article_title: Increasing Undergraduate Success: A Randomized Controlled Trial of "U-Pace" Instruction
citation: Fleming, R., Pedrick, L.E., Soiber, L., Kienzler, S., Fleming, R.R., & Reddy, D.M. (2018). Increasing undergraduate success: A randomized controlled trial of U-Pace instruction. Online Learning, 22(3), 175-191. https://doi.org/10.24059/olj.v22i3.1317
title: U-Pace instruction: an online instructional model integrating concept mastery and amplified assistance
description: U-Pace instruction is an online instructional model comprising two empirically supported components: concept mastery and amplified assistance. In concept mastery, "students typically master one content unit before progressing to a new content unit"; in U-Pace, students must score at least 90% on each unit quiz before advancing. Amplified assistance is "personalized support provided by the instructor to all students without them having to ask for help", delivered as weekly instructor-initiated email tailored from learning management system data. The RCT reported here found the combination, not either component alone, produced greater learning.
requirements: Instructors trained to implement the conditions with fidelity, following an implementation manual
Learning management system information about student engagement and performance available to instructors for tailoring assistance
Field-tested U-Pace templates for crafting support messages
constraints: Evaluated in a single course context (Introduction to Psychology), a limitation the authors state
Grades are determined differently in mastery versus nonmastery approaches, which the authors note as a limitation
target_learners: Undergraduates in gateway courses, including students at risk for college noncompletion
target_learning_goals: Academic success (final grades of A or B)
Learning measured independently of grades on a proctored cumulative exam
examples: In the RCT, U-Pace students worked through 24 content units, retaking quizzes with different questions after at least an hour, while receiving weekly personalized support emails
key_sources: Fleming, R., Pedrick, L.E., Soiber, L., Kienzler, S., Fleming, R.R., & Reddy, D.M. (2018). Increasing undergraduate success: A randomized controlled trial of U-Pace instruction. Online Learning, 22(3), 175-191. https://doi.org/10.24059/olj.v22i3.1317

article_title: Increasing Undergraduate Success: A Randomized Controlled Trial of "U-Pace" Instruction
citation: Fleming, R., Pedrick, L.E., Soiber, L., Kienzler, S., Fleming, R.R., & Reddy, D.M. (2018). Increasing undergraduate success: A randomized controlled trial of U-Pace instruction. Online Learning, 22(3), 175-191. https://doi.org/10.24059/olj.v22i3.1317
title: Field-tested U-Pace email templates for amplified assistance messages
description: The U-Pace instructors used "freely available, field-tested U-Pace templates" to craft proactive, personalized email support messages. The templates specified that messages should contain "help with concepts not yet mastered, behavior-based praise to shape student performance toward success, and elements to modify students' beliefs that they could be successful even if they were unsuccessful at the moment". Instructors tailored messages using time elapsed since the last quiz attempt and quiz scores from the learning management system.
requirements: Instructor access to learning management system data on student engagement and performance
Instructors trained to tailor messages in response to inferred student needs
constraints: Messages were evaluated for alignment with templates in this study's fidelity checks; effectiveness of templates alone was not separately tested
target_learners: Undergraduate students in online gateway courses
target_learning_goals: Sustained engagement and motivation toward mastering course content
Modified student beliefs about themselves as learners
examples: Fidelity checks every two weeks confirmed all U-Pace and amplified assistance students received instructor-initiated weekly support messages aligned with the templates
key_sources: Fleming, R., Pedrick, L.E., Soiber, L., Kienzler, S., Fleming, R.R., & Reddy, D.M. (2018). Increasing undergraduate success: A randomized controlled trial of U-Pace instruction. Online Learning, 22(3), 175-191. https://doi.org/10.24059/olj.v22i3.1317

article_title: U-Shaped development of Newtonian concepts: Implications for pedagogical design and research practice
citation: Camp, P. J. (2010). U-shaped Development of Newtonian Concepts: Implications for Pedagogical Design and Research Practice. Spelman College. https://spelman.edu
title: U-shaped development as a general feature of cognition: performance dips are byproducts of reorganization, not loss of competency
description: The article advances an explanatory framework in which U-shaped development — temporary apparent regression during learning — is a general feature of human cognition and learning, documented across language, artistic creativity, scientific reasoning and other domains. Its core mechanism is that "decrements as well as increments in such non-monotonic patterns in performance are byproducts of underlying monotonic improvements in memory and cognition", so that "Competencies, once learned, do not disappear but they are unusually fragile while understanding reorganizes into a more mature form". The article applies this framework to its Newtonian quiz data and contrasts it with an interference explanation offered elsewhere.
requirements: Explanations must account for retrograde performance in all circumstances where U-shaped development is observed, constraining the space of process-based explanations
constraints: The framework is presented as an interpretation of the data, with parts of the paper explicitly marked as Reflection intended to generate discussion rather than statements of fact
examples: The author documents the phenomenon across concept clusters in one LBD classroom and reviews prior observations ranging from balance-scale reasoning to vocabulary acquisition
key_sources: Camp, P. J. (2010). U-shaped Development of Newtonian Concepts: Implications for Pedagogical Design and Research Practice. Spelman College. https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.1647

article_title: A comprehensive modelling and experimental approach for damped oscillations in U-tubes via Easy JavaScript Simulations
citation: Fredy A. Orjuela, J. E. García-Farieta, Héctor J. Hortúa, E. Munevar. (2024). A comprehensive modeling and experimental approach for damped oscillations in U-tubes via Easy JavaScript Simulations. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09866
title: Linear damped-oscillation model of a liquid column in a U-tube with three damping regimes
description: The article develops a Newtonian model of a liquid column oscillating in a U-tube, treating gravity and a viscous damping term proportional to velocity, yielding the equation of motion ρSL d²y/dt² + b dy/dt + 2ρSgy = 0 with solution y(t) = Ae^(−γt) cos(ω_d t + δ). The model distinguishes three regimes: "When the damping is light, it holds that b < √ω20(2ρLS)2, the fluid oscillates while its amplitude decays exponentially", a critically damped case where the fluid does not oscillate and approaches equilibrium quickly, and an overdamped case where the fluid approaches equilibrium over a longer period of time.
requirements: Assumes gravity and viscous frictional resistance between fluid and tube walls, neglecting surface tension at the upper liquid surface
Assumes laminar and low speed flow so frictional forces are proportional to velocity
constraints: The linear velocity-dependence assumption breaks down after about six seconds in the experiment, attributed to capillary and non-linear viscosity effects
target_learning_goals: understanding damped oscillations and the physical laws associated with damped systems
examples: Figure 2 plots amplitude versus time for light, critical, and heavy damping parameter conditions
key_sources: Fredy A. Orjuela, J. E. García-Farieta, Héctor J. Hortúa, E. Munevar. (2024). A comprehensive modeling and experimental approach for damped oscillations in U-tubes via Easy JavaScript Simulations. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09866
